action_trace.summary: Generated 10 targeted interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (group-aware feature selection workflows), pain points (current workarounds and pipeline friction), and acceptance criteria (validation scenarios, nested CV support, backward compatibility). Questions decompose the SequentialFeatureSelector groups-parameter requirement into stakeholder impact, technical constraints, and success metrics.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (group-based CV workflows), pain points (current workaround limitations), and acceptance criteria (propagation through internal methods, error handling, backward compatibility). Questions decompose the SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter requirement into actionable clarifications on scope, validation, and trade-offs.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (group-based CV workflows), pain points (data leakage, incorrect rankings), and acceptance criteria (API behavior, edge cases, validation). Questions decompose the requirement to add groups parameter to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() by exploring context, impact, and success metrics.

End users need SequentialFeatureSelector to accept groups parameter in fit() to enable group-aware cross-validation for real-world scenarios involving multi-site data, temporal hierarchies, and stratified cohorts. Current limitation forces manual workarounds. Solution requires parameter propagation through _get_best_new_feature() to cross_val_score().

End-users require SequentialFeatureSelector to accept a groups parameter in fit() to enable group-based cross-validation strategies for hierarchical/multi-site datasets. This eliminates maintenance burden of custom implementations, prevents data leakage in grouped scenarios, and maintains backward compatibility through optional parameter design.

End-users require SequentialFeatureSelector to accept and propagate a groups parameter through fit() → _get_best_new_feature() → cross_val_score() to enable group-based cross-validation strategies for real-world hierarchical datasets (multi-site clinical data, batch-structured industrial data) while maintaining backward compatibility and eliminating the need for duplicate custom implementations.

Clarification needed on groups parameter optionality, backward compatibility guarantees, error handling for incompatible CV splitters, parameter propagation strategy, and documentation requirements for real-world group-based cross-validation scenarios.

Five clarification questions identify critical design decisions for groups parameter implementation: backward compatibility defaults, error handling strategy (early vs. lazy validation), validation timing, parameter optionality semantics, and internal propagation behavior. These decisions directly impact API usability, error messaging, and maintenance burden for data science teams using group-based cross-validation with SequentialFeatureSelector.

End-user raised 7 clarification questions decomposing the groups parameter feature into critical decision points: backward compatibility strategy (universal default vs. adaptive), validation timing (early vs. lazy), error handling scope (fail-fast vs. delegated), propagation chain completeness, optional vs. required semantics, None-with-group-aware-splitter behavior, and scope of non-grouped splitter handling. Chain-of-Thought analysis reveals these questions cluster around three core tensions: (1) backward compatibility vs. type safety, (2) validation responsibility (SequentialFeatureSelector vs. cross_val_score), (3) error signaling timing. Resolving these clarifications is prerequisite to unambiguous requirements specification.

End user confirms groups parameter requirement for group-based CV in SequentialFeatureSelector to support multi-site clinical datasets and prevent data leakage. Refined approach: optional groups parameter with early validation at fit() to detect cv splitter compatibility, propagating through internal methods to cross_val_score(), maintaining backward compatibility while eliminating parallel implementation burden.

End-user requirements confirmed and refined: Add optional groups parameter to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() with early validation at entry point to detect cv splitter group-support compatibility. Parameter propagates through _get_best_new_feature() to cross_val_score(). Maintains backward compatibility (default=None) while enabling GroupKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold for hierarchical datasets and eliminating parallel implementation maintenance burden.

End-user requirements for SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter addition are validated and refined. Groups parameter shall be optional (default=None), propagate through internal methods, and undergo early validation at fit() to raise TypeError for incompatible cv splitter types. This enables group-based cross-validation for multi-site datasets while preserving backward compatibility and eliminating parallel feature selection implementations.

Consolidated 5 structured elicitation records (IR-001 through IR-005) documenting the requirement to add an optional groups parameter to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() with early validation and propagation through internal methods. Records trace enduser pain points (multi-site datasets, data leakage, implementation burden) to validated solution (optional groups parameter, early validation at fit() entry, backward compatibility via None default). All records conform to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 functional/non-functional/constraint classification and include rationale linking to enduser confirmations.

Synthesized 7-item hierarchical requirements list prioritized by MoSCoW: 4 MUST (core groups parameter addition, propagation, early validation, backward compatibility), 2 SHOULD (documentation, testing), 1 COULD (enhanced error messaging). All items traced to interview records and end-user confirmations. Addresses multi-site/batch cross-validation pain points while preserving backward compatibility for non-grouped workflows.

Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: The Deployer must clarify infrastructure constraints (deployment environments, scalability limits, validation latency), security mandates (group audit trails, data leakage prevention logging), backward compatibility rollout strategy, error handling philosophy (fail-fast vs. lazy), integration points with upstream sklearn components, testing infrastructure availability, and documentation/knowledge transfer requirements. These eight targeted questions probe deployment feasibility, operational risk, and knowledge dissemination for the groups parameter feature across development, staging, and production contexts.

Seven targeted questions probing deployer constraints across infrastructure scalability, security/governance, backward compatibility enforcement, error handling observability, integration surface area, and validation performance trade-offs—grounded in the groups parameter propagation requirement chain (fit → _get_best_new_feature → cross_val_score) and early validation mandate from enduser confirmations.

Interviewer formulated 7 targeted questions probing infrastructure deployment environments, security/compliance mandates for group-based CV validation, scalability constraints on parameter propagation, backward compatibility impact on existing pipelines, error handling timing trade-offs (early vs. lazy validation), integration with existing monitoring frameworks, and rollout strategy for groups parameter adoption—anchoring deployment readiness assessment to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 life-cycle trade-off reasoning.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness: groups parameter addition imposes no external dependencies, negligible memory overhead (O(n)), and linear scalability. Early validation at fit() entry point recommended to detect group-incompatible splitters and raise TypeError immediately, preventing silent failures. Backward compatibility maintained via groups=None default. Deployment targets scikit-learn CI/CD (Python 3.8+, multi-platform). Documentation and unit test coverage required per REQ-005 and REQ-006.

Deployer confirms groups parameter addition to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() requires: (1) no infrastructure changes—parameter is in-memory array-like with O(1) passing overhead; (2) early TypeError validation at fit() entry point for incompatible splitters, leveraging existing cross_val_score() input validation; (3) O(n) memory scalability with no algorithmic complexity increase; (4) mandatory backward compatibility via groups=None default; (5) unmodified parameter propagation through fit() → _get_best_new_feature() → cross_val_score() call chain to enable GroupKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold strategies in multi-site datasets without operational cost increase.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness: groups parameter integrates into scikit-learn CI/CD (Python 3.8+, multi-platform) with O(n) linear scaling and O(1) per-call overhead; security mandates satisfied through existing cross_val_score() input validation; scalability targets met with no algorithmic complexity increase; operational procedures specify early validation at fit() entry point with TypeError for incompatible splitters, transparent parameter propagation, and universal groups=None backward compatibility default.

Seven clarifications needed to operationalize groups parameter deployment: (1) validation timing strategy (early vs lazy), (2) groups array immutability contract, (3) backward compatibility error handling edge case, (4) cv splitter capability detection mechanism, (5) groups parameter scope in internal methods, (6) TypeError message specificity, (7) performance regression baseline. All clarifications address infrastructure, security, and scalability concerns identified in deployer responses; resolution required before implementation commencement.

Deployer RaiseQuestionDeployer action identifies five operational clarifications needed before implementation: (1) validation timing strategy (early vs. deferred), (2) groups array immutability contract, (3) backward compatibility edge case handling, (4) error message specificity for incompatible splitters, (5) groups parameter type flexibility. All clarifications directly impact infrastructure deployment, security validation scope, and backward compatibility guarantees. Recommend enduser/architect confirmation on validation timing and error handling strategy before proceeding to code implementation.

Deployer requests five clarifications on validation timing strategy, groups array immutability contract, backward compatibility error handling, infrastructure dependency scope, and scalability thresholds to finalize implementation approach for groups parameter addition to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(). Chain-of-thought analysis reveals trade-offs between early validation (user feedback, computation prevention) vs. deferred validation (implementation simplicity), immutability contract (safety, predictability) vs. modification (memory optimization), and error-first strategy (data leakage prevention) vs. silent ignore (maximum backward compatibility). Decisions required before implementation phase.

Deployer confirms groups parameter addition to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() is deployment-ready. Early validation at fit() entry point detects group-aware splitter capability and raises TypeError if groups provided with incompatible splitter. Groups parameter is read-only, propagates through fit() → _get_best_new_feature() → cross_val_score() call chain, and maintains backward compatibility (groups=None default). Infrastructure, security, and scalability constraints satisfied. Implementation requires parameter addition, type detection logic, propagation plumbing, unit test coverage, and API documentation updates.

Deployer confirms groups parameter addition to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() with early validation at entry point, read-only propagation through _get_best_new_feature()→cross_val_score() call chain, backward compatibility via groups=None default, and infrastructure readiness for scikit-learn CI/CD pipeline with O(n) memory and O(1) overhead. Requires unit test coverage for group-aware/non-aware splitter combinations and comprehensive API documentation.

Deployer confirms groups parameter addition to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() with early validation at entry point, read-only propagation through _get_best_new_feature() → cross_val_score(), backward compatibility via groups=None default, infrastructure readiness for scikit-learn CI/CD, and security posture via inherited input validation. Requires API documentation and unit test coverage for groups parameter usage and error conditions.

Operating environment for SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter addition: Python 3.8+ on scikit-learn CI/CD (Linux/macOS/Windows); in-memory groups array passed by reference with O(n) scaling and O(1) per-call overhead; early validation at fit() entry point detecting group-aware splitter capability via hasattr/inspect checks; read-only parameter propagation through call chain; TypeError raised immediately when groups provided with incompatible splitters; backward compatibility preserved via groups=None default; existing cross_val_score() input validation inherited; no new external dependencies or network requirements.

Consolidated system requirements for SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter addition: optional groups parameter (default=None) with early validation at fit() entry point, unchanged propagation through internal call chain, TypeError for incompatible splitters, full backward compatibility, read-only parameter semantics, comprehensive API documentation, unit test coverage, Python 3.8+ CI/CD deployment, and inherited input validation security. Requirements address multi-site/batch cross-validation pain points while maintaining production stability and performance.

Selected UML Use Case Diagram as primary model to visualize Data Scientist actor interaction with SequentialFeatureSelector for group-based cross-validation workflows, complemented by SysML IBD for internal call-chain architecture and parametric diagram for backward compatibility constraints. This dual-model approach satisfies IEEE 830 functional requirements specification, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability, and resolves deployer clarifications on validation timing, parameter immutability, and backward compatibility edge cases through explicit architectural documentation.

Requirements model for sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter addition is VALIDATED and CONSISTENT. Three key requirements (add optional groups parameter, propagate through call chain, early validation with TypeError) are confirmed across all stakeholder responses. One critical conflict (validation timing) is RESOLVED in favor of early fit() entry-point validation. Three gaps identified (splitter detection mechanism, error message template, edge-case test coverage) are MITIGATED through existing cross_val_score() infrastructure and documented error handling. Model is ready for SysML IBD and UML Use Case diagram generation to visualize data flow and actor interactions.
